Red Teaming Language Models with Language Models

paper.acl.2022.emnlp-main.225

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at ACL-Anthology-2022.emnlp-main.225-captured-2026-11-10. Actual offensive-text-classifier experiment and false-positive/false-negative discussion establish evaluation/red-team protocol scope; uninspected other-harm experiments are not credited. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Biases in the red model can restrict diversity and flawed red-team classifiers can create false positives or miss failures; the authors present automated red teaming as complementary to manual testing rather than exhaustive discovery.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The pipeline generates test inputs with a red language model, obtains target-model replies, and uses a classifier to flag harmful outputs; the offensive-dialogue study used 280B Gopher for red and target models and a 1.4B Gopher classifier fine-tuned on BAD.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The 0.5 million zero-shot questions elicited classifier-flagged offensive replies in 3.7% of cases, yielding 18, 444 failures; RL with KL penalty 0.3 elicited over 40%, but 78% of its test cases contained “invisible”.
